options: Splitting one large task across multiple machines so they work on pieces of it simultaneously
Running a task twice on the same machine for accuracy
Storing a file in two different locations for backup
A synonym for exception handling
questions.explain: Twelve months of data across twelve machines in parallel finishes in roughly the time of one month, not twelve.

options: Running code where the data already lives, instead of moving the large data across the network to the code
Storing all data on a single central machine
A method for compressing data before transfer
A rule that data can only be stored in one specific geographic region
questions.explain: Moving a small piece of code is far cheaper than moving a huge dataset across a network.

questions.q: Why is moving computation to data usually better than moving data to computation?
options: Moving large datasets across a network is slow and is often the actual bottleneck in distributed systems
Data can never be moved between machines under any circumstances
Code is always larger than the datasets it processes
There is no real performance difference between the two approaches
questions.explain: Sending a few KB of code is dramatically cheaper than moving hundreds of gigabytes of data.

questions.q: What does fault tolerance mean in a distributed system?
options: If one machine fails mid-task, the work gets re-run elsewhere in the cluster instead of the entire job failing
The system prevents all hardware failures from ever occurring
Every machine in the cluster must never restart
Fault tolerance means the system ignores incorrect results silently
questions.explain: With enough machines running long enough, individual failures become a statistical certainty the system must plan for.

questions.q: Why does this lesson's general distributed computing concepts matter before learning Spark's specific architecture?
options: Spark's components (driver, cluster manager, executors) exist specifically to implement data locality and fault tolerance
Spark's architecture has no relationship to these general concepts
Distributed computing concepts only apply to Hadoop, never Spark
